### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. cerebral amyloid angiopathy, APP-related  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.428)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-445989)

**Proposed mechanism:** APP missense variant (HP:0002395) —DISRUPTS→ APP (HGNC:640); APP (HGNC:640) —LEADS_TO→ Amyloid precursor protein processing (GO:0001707); Amyloid precursor protein processing (GO:0001707) —PRODUCES→ Amyloid beta-42 (CHEBI:50901); Amyloid beta-42 (CHEBI:50901) —LEADS_TO→ Cognitive impairment (HP:0001263); Amyloid beta-42 (CHEBI:50901) —LEADS_TO→ Cerebral amyloid angiopathy (HP:0002395). Gain-of-function variants in APP lead to altered amyloid precursor protein processing, resulting in the accumulation of amyloid beta-42. This accumulation contributes to both cognitive impairment and cerebral amyloid angiopathy.

**How to falsify it:** Absence of amyloid beta-42 accumulation in the brain in individuals with APP variants linked to MONDO:0013999. _(variant: rs121917942)_

**Why it matters:** Targeting APP processing or amyloid beta-42 accumulation could offer therapeutic avenues for both conditions.

#### 2. cardiospondylocarpofacial syndrome  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.422)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-445989, Reactome:R-HSA-9645460)

**Proposed mechanism:** MAP3K7 (HGNC:6862) —DISRUPTS→ NF-kappaB signaling pathway (WP:WP461); NF-kappaB signaling pathway (WP:WP461) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal facial shape (HP:0000274); NF-kappaB signaling pathway (WP:WP461) —LEADS_TO→ Spondylometaphyseal dysplasia (HP:0008772). Haploinsufficiency of MAP3K7 disrupts the NF-kappaB signaling pathway, leading to the shared downstream phenotypes of abnormal facial shape and spondylometaphyseal dysplasia, characteristic of both MONDO:0013999 and cardiospondylocarpofacial syndrome.

**How to falsify it:** Absence of pathogenic variants in MAP3K7 in individuals with either MONDO:0013999 or cardiospondylocarpofacial syndrome, or identification of distinct causal genes and pathways for each disease that do not converge on NF-kappaB signaling. _(variant: rs11547431)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of MAP3K7 and NF-kappaB signaling in these distinct rare diseases could reveal common therapeutic targets for managing their overlapping skeletal and craniofacial manifestations.

#### 3. autoinflammatory disease, X-linked  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.386)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-445989)

**Proposed mechanism:** ALPK1 (HGNC:24405) —DISRUPTS→ NF-kappaB signaling pathway (WP:WP460); NF-kappaB signaling pathway (WP:WP460) —LEADS_TO→ Inflammatory response (HP:00114212); IKBKG (HGNC:5703) —DISRUPTS→ NF-kappaB signaling pathway (WP:WP460); NF-kappaB signaling pathway (WP:WP460) —LEADS_TO→ Autoinflammatory disease (HP:0012602). Loss of function in either ALPK1 or IKBKG leads to disruption of the NF-kappaB signaling pathway, resulting in aberrant inflammatory responses and contributing to the pathogenesis of their respective diseases.

**How to falsify it:** The absence of any shared downstream effects on the NF-kappaB signaling pathway in cellular or animal models of ALPK1 and IKBKG deficiency would falsify this hypothesis. Specifically, if mutations in ALPK1 do not impact NF-kappaB activation while IKBKG mutations do, despite both leading to inflammatory phenotypes. _(variant: The presence of common variants (AF > 0.01) in gnomAD within the coding regions of both ALPK1 and IKBKG that are not associated with either disease would weaken the hypothesis.)_

**Why it matters:** Targeting the NF-kappaB signaling pathway could offer a common therapeutic strategy for patients with either ALPK1- or IKBKG-related disorders, despite their distinct primary genetic causes.

#### 4. immunodeficiency, common variable, 10  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.385)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-445989)

**Proposed mechanism:** ALPK1 (HGNC:28513) —DISRUPTS→ NF-kappa B signaling pathway (WP:WP476); NF-kappa B signaling pathway (WP:WP476) —LEADS_TO→ Immunodeficiency (HP:0002705); NFKB2 (HGNC:7799) —DISRUPTS→ NF-kappa B signaling pathway (WP:WP476); NF-kappa B signaling pathway (WP:WP476) —LEADS_TO→ Common variable immunodeficiency (HP:0000783). Loss-of-function mutations in ALPK1 disrupt the NF-kappa B signaling pathway, leading to immunodeficiency. Similarly, loss-of-function mutations in NFKB2 also disrupt the NF-kappa B signaling pathway, leading to common variable immunodeficiency. The convergence on the NF-kappa B signaling pathway represents the shared mechanistic link.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that mutations in ALPK1 do not affect the NF-kappa B signaling pathway, or that mutations in NFKB2 do not impact immune cell function, would falsify this hypothesis. Additionally, if common variable immunodeficiency is shown to be caused by a gain-of-function of NFKB2, and MONDO:0013999 is loss-of-function, then the shared mechanism on the NF-kappa B pathway is invalidated. _(variant: Presence of pathogenic variants in gnomAD with a frequency > 0.01% for either ALPK1 or NFKB2.)_

**Why it matters:** Identifying a shared pathway (NF-kappa B signaling) offers potential therapeutic targets for both MONDO:0013999 and common variable immunodeficiency. Modulating this pathway could be a strategy to ameliorate immune defects in both conditions.

#### 5. immunodeficiency, common variable, 12  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.385)

**Proposed mechanism:** NFKB1 (HGNC:7774) —DISRUPTS→ NF-kappaB signaling pathway (WP:WP466); NF-kappaB signaling pathway (WP:WP466) —DECREASES→ Cytokine production (GO:0001816); NF-kappaB signaling pathway (WP:WP466) —DECREASES→ ALPK1 (HGNC:28723); ALPK1 (HGNC:28723) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal innate immune response (HP:0011223); Cytokine production (GO:0001816) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal B cell function (HP:0003317). **Proposed mechanism:** ALPK1 (HGNC:28516) —DISRUPTS→ NF-kappaB signaling pathway (WP:WP44); IKBKB (HGNC:5470) —DISRUPTS→ NF-kappaB signaling pathway (WP:WP44); NF-kappaB signaling pathway (WP:WP44) —LEADS_TO→ Immunodeficiency (HP:0002719). Loss-of-function mutations in ALPK1 (MONDO:0013999) and IKBKB (MONDO:0032599) both disrupt the NF-kappaB signaling pathway, leading to a shared phenotype of immunodeficiency.

**How to falsify it:** If genetic analysis reveals that mutations in ALPK1 and IKBKB affect entirely independent cellular processes that do not converge on the NF-kappaB signaling pathway, or if patients with loss-of-function mutations in one gene show normal function of the NF-kappaB pathway, this hypothesis would be falsified. _(variant: gnomAD allele frequency > 0.01 for pathogenic variants in ALPK1 or IKBKB)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of ALPK1 and IKBKB in the NF-kappaB pathway could reveal common therapeutic targets for different types of immunodeficiencies. Modulating this pathway could offer a unified strategy for immune system restoration or modulation.

#### 7. frontometaphyseal dysplasia 2  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.383)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-445989, Reactome:R-HSA-9645460)
